newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries open steady, tight ranges expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries open steady, tight ranges expected.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened largely unchanged on Thursday, as the light economic data schedule is expected to keep the market tightly range-bound.
The 30-year bond was at 94-10/32, unchanged from Wednesday, while its yield stood at 7.09 percent.

Jobless claims figures for the week ended April 19 are due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT and the Conference Board's Help Wanted Index for March is due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, but they are not expected to have a significant effect on Treasuries, unless far from expectations.
Claims are seen falling slightly to a 328,000 level, according to a Reuters poll of economists.

Meanwhile, the market continues to concentrate on supply. Wednesday's five-year note auction appreared to have gone well initially, but lack of follow-through buying contributed to the more than half-point fall in bond prices late in the session.

Dealers noted they were having trouble unloading the new securities. The distribution of the five-year notes and two-year notes, which were sold on Tuesday, continues this session with the hopes the cheaper levels will entice buying.
More supply is on the way this session, as the Treasury sells $13.75 billion 52-week bills at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT, but the bills ahould have little problem in finding buyers, traders said.
However, continued corporate supply could pressure Treasuries, some speculated.
Still, traders do not expect a breakout from the narrow ranges seen in recent sessions.

"It'll be choppy within those ranges and there's nothing more than that," said Kevin Sluder, head trader at First Chicago Capital Markets Inc. "We'll be stuck for a while. It is unfortunate but that is the reality for the time being."

Players said the market may get its cues from elsewhere this session, such as foreign exchange. The firmer dollar gave mild support to Treasuries in overseas trading during the night, as the dollar rose to 126.15 yen and 1.7195 marks.

But any activity is said to be dealer driven, as few retail accounts wish to take on big positions ahead of both this weekend's G7 meeting and Tuesday's all-important employment cost report for the first quarter.
In early trading, bill rates were unchanged to up one basis point.

Two-year notes were down 1/32 at 99-12/32, yielding 6.49 percent. Five-year notes were unchanged at 99-12/32 to yield 6.78 percent, and 10-year notes were down 2/32 at 95-16/32, yielding 6.89 percent.
